content.text:
Grow, from the skin of the back and flanks, a covering of hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors that replaces the brown bear's fur over the back and flanks: it grows in the skin as the brown bear's own covering there, not as pieces added on top; the fur stops at the covering's edge, and the belly and legs keep the brown bear's own fur; the covering is a carapace grown in the skin like an armadillo's, shaped like a beetle's two elytra: one domed dorsal shield from the shoulders to the hips, in two halves meeting at a midline seam, never scattered plates. Also grow a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rooted on the nasal bone like a rhinoceros horn, its base merging into the skin of the brow. Keep the pose, the head, the legs, the fur everywhere else, the background and everything else the same.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.
